findings.title: Information Leakage: baseline overwrite hides CAD changes
findings.why_it_matters: The exporter calculates R7 geometry scalars and then replaces every original R5 field outside a short exception list. If a future M222 CAD edit changes an inherited wire length, native lead length, or bond footprint, the thermal CSV can continue to report the R5 value and the CAD-coupled comparison becomes stale without an error.
evidence: packages/temper-thermal/studies/glass_sensor/revision7/mechanical/build.py:350-360: The loop copies original[key] into row[key] for every R5 field outside seven exceptions, after CAD-derived row.update calls at lines 310-337.

packages/temper-thermal/studies/glass_sensor/revision7/mechanical/README.md:33: The scalar contract is described as actual rest-pose geometry, with unchanged dimensions inherited and modified volumes derived from R7 solids.
findings.suggested_fix: For each inherited R5 scalar that is also measured from R7 solids, assert agreement with the CAD-derived value before carrying forward the baseline text. Keep the explicit seven changed fields as CAD values, and fail when a newly changed M222 field has not been declared as such.
